title: Dropdown form submits can vanish when the menu unmounts
summary: A native form placed inside a dropdown, popover, command menu, or context menu can lose its submit path if the menu closes and unmounts before the browser or framework dispatches the submit/mutation. The UI may look clicked while no API request is sent.
ai_value: Helps agents diagnose missing mutations in menu-driven UI actions without over-focusing on backend routes, auth, or validation when the frontend never sent the request.

contexts: React, Vue, Svelte, or similar component UIs with dropdown, popover, context-menu, command-menu, or modal actions
Menu items implemented as forms, submit buttons, server actions, or framework action helpers
User reports that clicking a menu action closes the menu but produces no backend effect

trigger_signals.description: A button or menu item closes a dropdown immediately and no network request appears for the intended action.
trigger_signals.pattern: dropdown|popover|menu|context menu|no request|no API call|submit|form action
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Inspect whether the form or submit button unmounts before submit/mutation dispatch.

trigger_signals.description: Backend route, validation, and auth tests pass, but the real UI action has no server log or request trace.
trigger_signals.pattern: route passes|server action works|no server log|clicked but nothing happened
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Suspect frontend event lifetime or component unmount rather than backend behavior.

negative_signals.description: The network request is sent and receives a 4xx/5xx or validation response.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Then the problem is downstream of event dispatch, such as auth, payload shape, validation, or backend logic.

negative_signals.description: The menu component keeps the form mounted until the submit promise is started or awaited, and tests prove the request fires before close.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Unmount loss is unlikely when lifecycle ordering is explicitly controlled and verified.

common_wrong_assumptions: If a submit button was clicked, the browser definitely sent the form submit.
A menu closing after click means the action succeeded or at least reached the backend.
Missing mutation effects are most likely a route, auth, or database bug.
Native forms are always safer than explicit fetch calls inside transient menu components.

first_checks.check: Use the browser network tab or test mock to prove whether the action request is sent before debugging the backend.
first_checks.why: A vanished submit leaves no request; backend inspection cannot explain an event that never left the client.

first_checks.check: Inspect whether the menu closes, route changes, or state update unmounts the form synchronously in the same click path.
first_checks.why: Transient component lifecycle can interrupt native form/server-action submission.

first_checks.check: Add a regression test that clicks the actual menu item and asserts the mutation function or network request is called.
first_checks.why: Route-only tests miss the frontend event lifetime bug.

decision_rules.condition: The menu action unmounts the form before a submit or mutation is observed.
decision_rules.then: Use an explicit click handler/fetch/server-action call that starts before closing the menu, or defer menu close until submit has been dispatched/awaited.

decision_rules.condition: A regression test only exercises the backend route or action helper directly.
decision_rules.then: Add a component or browser test that opens the dropdown, clicks the menu action, and observes the request/mutation call.

do_not: Do not assume a clicked native form inside a transient dropdown sent a request unless the network/log evidence shows it.
Do not debug backend persistence first when the UI action has no request trace.
Do not expose private UI labels, account names, URLs, or customer data in public candidate examples.

agent_directives.preferred_next_step: When a dropdown/menu action appears to do nothing, prove request dispatch in the actual UI path; if absent, make mutation dispatch explicit or keep the form mounted through submit.

risk.notes: This is a frontend event-lifecycle trap. Production mutations, auth, data deletion, or customer-visible behavior changes still need their ordinary gates.

sources.supports: A private frontend session found that menu-contained native forms closed/unmounted before submit reached the API; replacing the path with explicit request dispatch fixed the missing mutation.
